trial_court: Family Court-cum-Additional District Judge, Anantapuramu (F.C.O.P.No.32 of 2018)
case_name: P.Shanthi Kiran vs State Of Ap on 17 June, 2020

parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Andhra Pradesh, rep. by Public Prosecutor, High Court Buildings, Amaravati & Anr. — Respondents

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner's marriage was annulled by a decree of nullity passed under Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. She claimed monthly maintenance under Section 125 Cr.P.C., but the trial court dismissed her petition saying she cannot be termed as a wife or divorcee as contemplated under Section 125 Cr.P.C.

legal_principles.principle: Dissolution of marriage on divorce should not be equated to a decree of nullity.
legal_principles.held: This Court did not accept the said contention. After considering the legal effect of the decrees passed under Sections 11 and 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act, this Court held as follows: 'Dissolution of marriage as a sequel to divorce should not be equated to decree of nullity'.

legal_principles.principle: The distinction between dissolution of marriage on divorce and nullity of marriage is clearly discernible.
legal_principles.held: It is further held that the distinction between dissolution of marriage on divorce and nullity of marriage is clearly discernible.

legal_principles.principle: The mere decree for divorce does not result in fanning the wings and getting away from the tie unless the conditions stipulated in Section 15 are fulfilled.
legal_principles.held: In the event of dissolution of marriage on divorce, the remarriage by either party is intertwined by certain strings and conditions and the mere decree for divorce does not result in fanning the wings and getting away from the tie unless the conditions stipulated in Section 15 are fulfilled.

legal_principles.principle: The Court below is not competent to grant maintenance under Section 125 Cr.P.C. in the event of a decree for nullity.
legal_principles.held: It is finally held that in view of the decree of nullity of the marriage that was passed, the Court below is not competent to grant maintenance under Section 125 Cr.P.C.

legal_principles.principle: The benefit of the explanation has to be extended even to the woman whose marriage was annulled by a decree of nullity under Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: He would submit that despite passing of decree of annulment of marriage that Section 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act still preserves the right of a woman to claim maintenance and the statute also retained the jurisdiction of the Court passing the said decree for the purpose of granting maintenance either at the time of passing the said decree or even subsequent thereto.

outcome.final_order: The petition filed by the revision petitioner was dismissed on the ground that she cannot be termed as a wife or divorcee as contemplated under Section 125 Cr.P.C.
